content.text:
# iwe bare front matter support

## Problem

iwe requires `---` fenced YAML front matter. Some wiki systems (e.g., TibbitWiki) use bare RFC 822-style headers — `key: value` lines at the top of the file, separated from body by a blank line, no delimiters. The content is valid YAML; only the framing differs.

## Design

### Detection rule

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled in config and the file does not start with `---`:
- Check if the first line starts with `title: `
- If so, all lines up to the first blank line are treated as front matter
- Parse that block as YAML

If the first line is not `title: `, no bare front matter is detected; the file is parsed normally.

The `title:` requirement avoids false positives (e.g., prose starting with `Something: explanation`). No key whitelist is needed — `title` as a mandatory first key is sufficient, and additional keys can be added freely over time.

### Config

Add `bare_frontmatter = true` to `.iwe/config.toml` under `[markdown]`. Default: `false` (current behavior preserved).

### Reader changes

In `MarkdownReader::document()` (or the events reader), before passing content to pulldown_cmark:
- If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled, detect bare headers per the rule above
- Wrap the detected block with `---` delimiters so pulldown_cmark parses it as a metadata block
- The rest of the pipeline (metadata storage, title extraction, graph) works unchanged

### Writer changes

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled:
- Emit metadata as bare `key: value` lines followed by a blank line — no `---` fences
- This preserves round-trip compatibility with systems that don't understand YAML front matter delimiters

### Scope of changes

- `crates/liwe/src/model/config.rs` — add `bare_frontmatter` field
- `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs` or `crates/liwe/src/markdown/reader.rs` — pre-process content
- `crates/liwe/src/markdown/writer.rs` — conditional fence suppression
- Tests for: detection, round-trip, no false positive on prose, interaction with `---` fenced files

## Future: metadata querying

Once front matter is reliably parsed (bare or fenced), add `--meta key=value` filtering to `iwe find`. This enables task tracking via front matter fields like `status: active`, `depends: concurrency-design`, etc., queryable from the CLI.

## Compatibility note

TibbitWiki uses four keys: `title`, `tags`, `created`, `modified`. Enabling `bare_frontmatter` in an iwe workspace pointing at wiki notes would let iwe read them natively. The writer would emit bare headers, preserving compatibility with the wiki.
# iwe Enhancements — Implementation Plan

Source spec: `ENHANCEMENTS_SPEC.md`. Codebase reading was scoped to the files
the spec touches; line numbers below refer to current `main`.

The spec lists four work items; only the three iwe-internal ones are in
scope here. The task wrapper (item 4) is a separate shell tool and is not
covered by this Rust implementation plan.

---

## Part 1 — Implementation Plan

The order below matches the spec's "Implementation order" and respects the
internal dependencies (config struct → reader/writer → find filter → virtual
nodes).

### Phase 0 — Config plumbing (prerequisite for everything)

**File: `crates/liwe/src/model/config.rs`**

- `MarkdownOptions` (defined L19–27): add
  `#[serde(default)] pub bare_frontmatter: bool` field. Update
  `Default for MarkdownOptions` (L29–39) to set `bare_frontmatter: false`.
- `LibraryOptions` (L158–166): add
  `#[serde(default)] pub virtual_directories: bool`. Update
  `Default for LibraryOptions` (L174–185) to `virtual_directories: false`.
- `migrate()` (L559–): add a v3→v4 migration that just bumps the version and
  leaves both new fields absent (defaults apply). Bump
  `Configuration.version` ceiling, add `set_config_version(..., 4)` branch.
  This keeps existing `.iwe/config.toml` files round-tripping cleanly.
- `Configuration::template()` (L318–): no change needed (defaults are off);
  optionally add commented-out hints in the template TOML.

**Tests to add (`crates/liwe/tests/config_migration_test.rs`):**

- `migrates_v3_to_v4_adds_no_keys`: existing v3 config parses, version
  becomes 4, `bare_frontmatter` and `virtual_directories` both `false`.
- `parses_bare_frontmatter_true`.
- `parses_virtual_directories_true`.

**Dependencies:** none. Must land before Phases 1, 2, and 3 because they
read these fields.

---

### Phase 1 — Bare front matter support

#### 1a. Reader: pre-wrap bare headers with `---`

**File: `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs`** (`MarkdownReader::document`, L26–33)

This is the cleanest injection point — it owns the `&str` content right
before it goes into `MarkdownEventsReader::read`. Add a helper:

```rust
fn wrap_bare_frontmatter(content: &str) -> Cow<'_, str> { ... }
```

Logic, gated on `markdown_options.bare_frontmatter`:

1. If `content` starts with `---` (optionally preceded by a UTF-8 BOM /
   leading whitespace? — see Open Question Q1) → return `Borrowed`.
2. Find first line. If it does not start with `title: ` (literal, including
   the space) → return `Borrowed`.
3. Find the index of the first blank line (`\n\n` or `\r\n\r\n`, or EOF).
4. Split into `header_block` and `rest`. Return
   `Owned(format!("---\n{header_block}\n---\n\n{rest}"))`.

Then `MarkdownReader::document` calls `reader.read(&wrapped)` instead of
`reader.read(content)`. The downstream pipeline already handles
`MetadataBlock` events (see `reader.rs` L356, L386 — the
`Tag::MetadataBlock(_)` arms toggle `metadata_block`, and the `Text` arm
captures the YAML into `self.metadata`). No other reader changes required.

#### 1b. Writer: emit bare headers when configured

# iwe bare front matter support

## Problem

iwe requires `---` fenced YAML front matter. Some wiki systems (e.g., TibbitWiki) use bare RFC 822-style headers — `key: value` lines at the top of the file, separated from body by a blank line, no delimiters. The content is valid YAML; only the framing differs.

## Design

### Detection rule

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled in config and the file does not start with `---`:
- Check if the first line starts with `title: `
- If so, all lines up to the first blank line are treated as front matter
- Parse that block as YAML

If the first line is not `title: `, no bare front matter is detected; the file is parsed normally.

The `title:` requirement avoids false positives (e.g., prose starting with `Something: explanation`). No key whitelist is needed — `title` as a mandatory first key is sufficient, and additional keys can be added freely over time.

### Config

Add `bare_frontmatter = true` to `.iwe/config.toml` under `[markdown]`. Default: `false` (current behavior preserved).

### Reader changes

In `MarkdownReader::document()` (or the events reader), before passing content to pulldown_cmark:
- If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled, detect bare headers per the rule above
- Wrap the detected block with `---` delimiters so pulldown_cmark parses it as a metadata block
- The rest of the pipeline (metadata storage, title extraction, graph) works unchanged

### Writer changes

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled:
- Emit metadata as bare `key: value` lines followed by a blank line — no `---` fences
- This preserves round-trip compatibility with systems that don't understand YAML front matter delimiters

### Scope of changes

- `crates/liwe/src/model/config.rs` — add `bare_frontmatter` field
- `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs` or `crates/liwe/src/markdown/reader.rs` — pre-process content
- `crates/liwe/src/markdown/writer.rs` — conditional fence suppression
- Tests for: detection, round-trip, no false positive on prose, interaction with `---` fenced files

## Future: metadata querying

Once front matter is reliably parsed (bare or fenced), add `--meta key=value` filtering to `iwe find`. This enables task tracking via front matter fields like `status: active`, `depends: concurrency-design`, etc., queryable from the CLI.

## Compatibility note

TibbitWiki uses four keys: `title`, `tags`, `created`, `modified`. Enabling `bare_frontmatter` in an iwe workspace pointing at wiki notes would let iwe read them natively. The writer would emit bare headers, preserving compatibility with the wiki.

content.text: Updated (877 chars)

Diagnosed and fixed.

## Root cause

Bare frontmatter is converted into fenced YAML before passing to `pulldown-cmark`. In the version under test, `wrap_bare_frontmatter()` cleaned the detected header block by dropping lines that start with a space.

That broke YAML sequences in bare frontmatter:

```yaml
title: Task A
depends:
  - foo
  - bar
```

The indented sequence items were removed before metadata parsing, so the stored metadata became effectively:

```yaml
title: Task A
depends:
```

Then `iwe find --meta depends=foo` parsed `depends` as non-sequence/null and returned no match. Fenced YAML did not go through this bare-wrapper cleanup path, so fenced documents continued to work.

## Fix

Changed `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs` so `wrap_bare_frontmatter()` preserves indentation inside the header block and only trims trailing whitespace from the whole header:

```rust
let cleaned_header = header.trim_end();
```

This keeps YAML sequences intact while avoiding extra trailing blank/space before the generated closing `---`.

## Regression test

Added a regression test in `crates/liwe/tests/find_metadata_test.rs`:

```rust
#[test]
fn value_in_bare_yaml_sequence_matches()
```

It imports a bare-frontmatter document with:

```yaml
depends:
  - foo
  - bar
```

and verifies metadata filtering for `depends=foo` returns the document.

## Verification

Ran:

```bash
cargo test -p liwe --test find_metadata_test value_in_bare_yaml_sequence_matches
cargo test
```

Both passed.

I also checked formatting for the files touched with:

```bash
rustfmt --check crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs crates/liwe/tests/find_metadata_test.rs
```

Passed.

Changes are left uncommitted for review.
